articles.summary: Ivan Perisic has stunned Portugal in the World Cup Round of 32.
articles.content:
Former Tottenham winger Perisic gives Croatia lead over Portugal before Ronaldo has goal ruled out

Ivan Perisic has stunned Portugal in the World Cup Round of 32.

Last Update:

37-year-old Ivan Perisic has given Croatia a shock lead over Portugal in the World Cup Round of 32.

The former Tottenham man was on hand early in the second half, picking up the ball unmarked at the back post before rifling past goalkeeper Diogo Costa.

It was the culmination of a good spell from Croatia, who had been the less dominant side in the first half.

But less than 10 minutes into the second period, the PSV Eindhoven man sparked wild celebrations among his team-mates and the heavily outnumbered fans in the stadium.

At half-time Portugal had managed nine shots, but only one had found the target.

Cristiano Ronaldo had gone close several times, just missing a number of headers from teasing crosses.

He also had a goal ruled out for a marginal offside call.

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes also had two chances to put Portugal ahead in the match, only to be denied on both occassions.

Now, Ronaldo and Co must find a way to mount a comeback, or suffer a shock exit at the first knockout round.

It could also mark the end of Ronaldo’s international career, with reports emerging earlier in the day that he will retire from Portugal duties after the tournament.

articles.title: Tuchel reveals Rice in ‘terrible pain’ during England’s win over DR Congo
articles.summary: Declan Rice is continuing to play through injury during England's Word Cup run.
articles.content:
Tuchel reveals Rice in ‘terrible pain’ during England’s win over DR Congo

Declan Rice is continuing to play through injury during England's Word Cup run.

Last Update:

Thomas Tuchel says Declan Rice is expected to be available for England’s World Cup last-16 clash with Mexico despite the midfielder playing through what the manager described as “terrible pain” against DR Congo.

Rice has been managing neural pain in his hamstring since Christmas and has required careful monitoring throughout the tournament.

The Arsenal midfielder was withdrawn as a precaution during England’s opening match against Croatia before returning against Ghana. He then sat out the victory over Panama after suffering a calf injury but was back in the starting line-up for Wednesday’s win.

Tuchel revealed the extent of Rice’s discomfort after the match.

“I asked him very late and he said, ‘I can do it for the team, but I am in terrible pain,'” Tuchel said.

“When Declan tells you that he is in terrible pain, then you know he cannot take it anymore, so he was grateful that we took him off.”

Table of Contents

Tuchel confident Rice can continue

Rice was substituted in stoppage time after another influential display, having even filled in at right-back during the closing stages as England dealt with several defensive absences.

Despite concerns over his ongoing nerve issue, Tuchel believes the midfielder can continue to manage the problem throughout the tournament.

“He just said after the game it’s not an issue, he will recover, so there is no injury,” Tuchel said.

“It’s more nerval pain.”

Asked whether Rice could continue going from game to game, the England boss replied: “He can, yeah.”

James and Quansah remain doubts

England’s biggest injury concerns continue to centre on defenders Reece James and Jarell Quansah.

James has not featured since suffering a hamstring injury against Ghana, while Quansah picked up an ankle problem after deputising at right-back against Panama.

Tuchel confirmed both players are making progress but stopped short of guaranteeing their involvement against Mexico.

“They are getting close. They are getting closer and closer. I saw them on the pitch,” he said.

“In the nature of their injury, Jarell is a little bit ahead of Reecey. But the race was close even to make it into the match squad this time.”

Neither player took part in England’s recovery session in Kansas City following the win over DR Congo, leaving doubts over their availability for Sunday’s match at the Estadio Azteca.

Agent of Enzo Fernandez confirms midfielder exploring move away from Chelsea this summer

Enzo Fernandez could leave Chelsea this summer.

Last Update:

Enzo Fernandez’s agent has confirmed the Chelsea midfielder is considering his options ahead of the summer transfer window, casting uncertainty over his long-term future at Stamford Bridge.

The Argentina international is currently focused on World Cup duty, but discussions are taking place behind the scenes regarding a potential move away from West London.

Fernandez remains under contract until 2032 and the club are not actively seeking to sell one of their key players, although speculation surrounding his future has continued to grow.

His representative, Javier Pastore, suggested that while no deal is close, opportunities are being explored.

“Today the player is calmly thinking about the national team,” Pastore said.

“He is only thinking about that and we are looking at possibilities to leave Chelsea, but there is nothing firm or confirmed at any club.”

Table of Contents

Real Madrid links continue

Fernandez has frequently been linked with Real Madrid and those rumours intensified after comments he made during the March international break.

The midfielder admitted at the time that he liked the Spanish giants, remarks which reportedly led to him being left out of Chelsea’s next two matches.

Pastore dismissed suggestions that Fernandez’s visits to Madrid should be interpreted as a sign that a transfer is imminent.

“He has many friends there, and he is very close friends with Julian Alvarez,” he said.

“And I also live in Madrid. Every time he travelled, he travelled to see me and to sort out work-related matters.”

Chelsea keen to keep key midfielder

Chelsea remain reluctant to lose Fernandez, who has become a central figure since arriving from Benfica in a club-record deal worth £107m in February 2023.

The 25-year-old has contributed 19 goals and 17 assists in 117 Premier League appearances and is viewed as an important part of the club’s future plans.

Sources indicate Chelsea expect Fernandez to return for pre-season training as scheduled following his post-World Cup break.

The uncertainty comes during a busy summer for the Blues, with new manager Xabi Alonso beginning work at the club and recruitment plans already underway.

Chelsea are continuing their efforts to strengthen the squad, with interest in Sunderland midfielder Granit Xhaka among the moves being explored.
